prompt: Watch a conversation grow against a small fixed context window (simulated at 4 "slots" for this example):

steps.label: Turn 1
steps.content: Window: [Msg 1]. One message in, plenty of room left. Everything sent so far fits easily.

steps.label: Turn 2
steps.content: Window: [Msg 1] [Msg 2]. Every new turn resends the whole conversation so far, plus the new message — the app is doing that resending, not the model remembering.

steps.label: Turn 3
steps.content: Window: [Msg 1] [Msg 2] [Msg 3]. Still fits — but notice the request is getting bigger (and more expensive) each turn, since the whole history goes along for the ride every time.

steps.label: Turn 4
steps.content: Window: [Msg 1] [Msg 2] [Msg 3] [Msg 4]. The window is now full at this simulated 4-slot size.

steps.label: Turn 5
steps.content: Window: [Msg 2] [Msg 3] [Msg 4] [Msg 5]. Msg 1 just got pushed out to make room. If Msg 1 contained something important — an instruction, a fact you told it — the model genuinely can't see it anymore. That's the 'it forgot what I said' moment, and it's a window-size problem, not a memory problem.
